advice: Experiment: compare the current single `sera_libxsmm_512(parameters)` call with sixteen `sera_libxsmm_panel32` calls, one per 32-row band. In `gemm`’s `n == 512` branch, initialize a zeroed 22-slot parameter array once; for each `r = 0, 32, ..., 480`, set `[4]=B`, `[10]=A+(size_t)r*512`, and `[16]=C+(size_t)r*512`, then call the helper. Keep all other slots zero and preserve the existing fallback. This tests whether the narrower helper’s packing and ZA work outweigh sixteen function/streaming-region entries and exits. It is a hypothesis only; no speedup is established.
risks: The extra calls and SME transitions may outweigh any benefit from the helper’s smaller panel. Packing still occurs within each call and all of it counts in the benchmark. Pointer offsets, parameter slots, and disjoint band coverage must match the documented column-major primitive ABI. The helper’s availability does not establish a full-GEMM win.
